claim: CGEL gives bare NPs and NPs with the as the adjective-embellishment patterns for names, and treats selection of a manifestation as a secondary use.
evidence_summary: Two reports from 2001 have a visibly shaken Giuliani and a visibly-shaken Yuri Lutsenko. CBS has already named Giuliani and described his emotional state before the indefinite NP.
finding: The article can accompany an adjective that characterizes an already identified bearer. An analysis in terms of manifestations would need an independent reason to posit selection of a stage here.
proposed_wording: Nonrestrictive adjectival dependents can occur in bare NPs and with the. With an adjective describing the bearer’s state on an occasion, a/an is also available.
inference: Does a/an with a modified personal name require the NP to select a bearer, counterpart or manifestation?

evidence.source: John Payne and Rodney Huddleston (2002). Nouns and noun phrases. The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language, 323–523.
evidence.passage: Ch. 5 §20.3, p. 520 [5ii], lists bare and the-marked NPs as the two patterns of adjective embellishment. §20.4 [8] treats selection of a manifestation as a secondary use.
evidence.example: The inimitable Oscar Wilde illustrates embellishment. The young Isaac Newton illustrates a restrictive reading.
evidence.establishes: The contrast turns on the modifier’s contribution. Neither example tests a/an in an embellishment.

evidence.source: CBS News. No Answers In NYC Fire. 18 June 2001.
evidence.passage: Ch. 5 §20.3, p. 520 [5ii], lists bare and the-marked NPs as the two patterns of adjective embellishment. §20.4 [8] treats selection of a manifestation as a secondary use.
evidence.example: A visibly shaken Giuliani noted the tragic circumstances during a hospital press conference.
evidence.establishes: The article accompanies an adjective that characterizes the same Giuliani already identified by name and office. The context provides no explicit contrast between stages.
evidence.locator: CBS News, paragraph before Giuliani’s Father’s Day quotation.

evidence.source: Congressional Record, 1 March 2001, quoting an international news report.
evidence.passage: Ch. 5 §20.3, p. 520 [5ii], lists bare and the-marked NPs as the two patterns of adjective embellishment. §20.4 [8] treats selection of a manifestation as a secondary use.
evidence.example: The speech tag uses a visibly-shaken Yuri Lutsenko. A later paragraph continues with surname-only reference.
evidence.establishes: A separate pre-2002 source attests the construction, this time with a full personal name.
evidence.locator: House, p. H607, report on Kiev tent camp.

evidence.source: Tamás Halm (2022). Modified pronouns and split agreement: the syntax of virtual performatives. NELS 52, 319–329.
evidence.passage: Ch. 5 §20.3, p. 520 [5ii], lists bare and the-marked NPs as the two patterns of adjective embellishment. §20.4 [8] treats selection of a manifestation as a secondary use.
evidence.example: Halm describes indefinite article plus adjective and name with visibly irritated Mr Andrews. He gives corresponding article-marked pronoun examples.
evidence.establishes: Independent analysis treats the adjective as nonrestrictive characterization. A stricter theory of manifestations requires a test that does not presuppose the article defines the reading.
